Veneers are matched for proper balance and consistency. Veneers are available flat cut or quarter cut, except for Oak, which is rift cut. Refer to the Surface Materials Reference Manual for descriptions of each cut.

Tip (wood trims): Answer panel wood trims are only available with quarter-cut finishes with the exception of maple finishes. Maple on wood trims is only available with flat-cut finishes. For ordering simplicity, both flat-cut and quarter-cut finishes can be specified on panel trims. However, for all finishes except maple, if a flat-cut finish is selected, the trims will have the coordinating quarter-cut finish. For maple finishes, if quarter-cut is selected, the trims will have the coordinating flat-cut finish. Blending panel trims with other wood products that have flat-cut finishes may be visually acceptable for most applications. If a more exact match is desired for non-maple finishes, please specify quarter-cut finishes for the entire project. If a more exact match is desired for maple finishes, please specify flat-cut finishes for the entire project.
Open-pore finish is a medium gloss finish that leaves the wood grain texture visible to the eye and distinguishable to the touch.

Full-fill finish is a medium-gloss finish that completely fills the grain texture, yet allows the grain pattern to be seen. The wood has a lustrous, satiny look, and it is smooth to the touch. This finish is available on the wood worksurface or field-installed top only.

*Clear-coat veneer sign-off: To ensure an understanding of the color ranges and characteristic variations of natural veneer, a sign-off sheet is required prior to orders being accepted for this clear-coat finish. The sign-off sheet is available through Steelcase advertising stock. Please use form number 09-0000756 for 3042, 05-0001370 for 3222 and 3224. (Applies to veneers marked with * : 3522, 3524, 3042, 3222, 3224.)

Wood is a natural material and variations will occur in color, grain and texture; these are not considered defects. All wood products will darken with age and exposure to ultraviolet light, especially cherry and maple veneer; rearrange desk accessories periodically to ensure even aging. Storage guidelines: do not store products in trailers; store in areas that simulate office temperatures (60°F to 90°F) and constant, office-like humidity; keep product away from light and cover products.

Composite Veneer: Composite veneers are an engineered wood intended to create specific grain patterns and characteristics. They are pre-stained and finished with Steelcase's Clarity water-borne UV topcoat. Only open-pore finishes are available on composite wood. Composite veneer and matching edge bands are available on most Steelcase brand products. Composites, for use as a solid nosing substitute, are not available. Steelcase does not recommend mixing composite veneers with natural solid nosings because composite and natural wood grain and color matching are rarely compatible. Composite veneers are Graded-In as Wood Group 1 pricing. Note: consult the composite sign-off sheet, form number 14-0000141; a sign-off sheet is required prior to orders being accepted for composite projects.

Premium Veneers: A selection of Premium veneers is available on most Steelcase brand products, as close to standard leadtimes as possible; all orders scheduled individually and leadtimes vary. The collection is Graded-In as Wood Group 2 and Wood Group 3, and supported like standard veneers. See the Steelcase surface materials section on village.steelcase.com. All premium veneers are in clear-coat. Sign-off sheet required prior to orders: form number 09-0000755 for 3032, 09-0000757 for 3052, 09-0000758 for 3832, and 09-0000759 for 3842.

The $425 fee covers formulating the Customiz color finish and applies regardless of whether an order is placed. An approval form must be signed to indicate customer acceptance of the Customiz match. A $5,000 initiation fee is charged prior to first order entry; it activates the finish for unlimited use on any Steelcase product for an 18 month period. After 18 months the finish may be reactivated for another 18 months for a $1,000 fee at any point within five years after the $5,000 initiation fee was paid; if not reactivated within five years, the finish is culled and the $5,000 initiation fee applies again. All style number related Customiz charges products are no cost as of April 2014. The matching and initiation fees are not discountable. Customiz stain takes 10 days to formulate. workstationRules.text: 30"D straight, tapered, and transition cantilevered worksurfaces require additional floor support along the front edge, such as a pedestal, end panel, post leg, side support bracket, or an adjacent return worksurface.
Taper-flat worksurfaces can be supported at the larger end with a side support bracket and a post leg. If the larger end is 30"D, a 24"D end panel can also be used.

3 mm edge bullet peninsula, jetty, and bubble jetty worksurfaces can be supported two ways: (a) a cantilever, a center support panel and a column; or (b) a cantilever, a side support bracket, and two post legs.

A center support panel should not be used (unfinished top edge would be exposed) for: bullet peninsula with P-edge, jetty with P-edge, bubble jetty with P-edge, angled peninsula with 3 mm edge and 1/2" cord drop. Use a cantilever, a side support bracket, and two post legs instead.

Linking peninsula and linking worksurfaces with 3" notch accommodate Answer panels. Legs and cantilevers or column and cantilevers must be used to support linking peninsula worksurfaces. One leg and two cantilevers must be used to support linking worksurfaces.
3 mm edge visitor worksurfaces must be supported by either a cantilever and a center support panel, or by a cantilever, a side support bracket, and a leg.

In P-edge profile worksurface applications (visitor), a side support bracket, a cantilever, and a leg must be used for support; a center support panel should not be used because its unfinished top edge would be exposed.

Panel-supported applications can use: closed loop, open loop, half loop, intermediate support, off-module worksurface-to-panel connector, side support brackets, cantilever with tie plate, end panel, standing-height end panel, support plate, center support panel with tie plate, standing-height center support panel with tie plate, columns or legs, Universal pedestal with filler, Universal lateral file with underworksurface lateral file filler.

Tip: Selected worksurfaces with P-edge profile include alignment slots to accept cabby legs for column support: use two legs for panel-mounted spanner, bullet peninsula, linking peninsula, jetty, and bubble jetty worksurfaces; use one leg for visitor and linking worksurfaces.

Answer Freestanding desk applications can use: end supports, peninsula supports, corner support, columns and legs, closed loop or open loop, modesty panels, pedestals, lateral files and storage cabinets (see Answer Freestanding Specification Guide).
Answer Freestanding peninsula support is not compatible with P-edge bullet peninsula, jetty, or bubble jetty worksurfaces. Legs or other alternate supports are recommended.

Leg-based applications can use: closed loop, open loop, intermediate support, post legs, double post leg, double post C-leg, support plate. Pedestal can also be used in leg-based freestanding installations.

Long worksurface spans must be supported with cantilevers, pedestals, legs, or other supports at least every 54". Reinforcing channel (TS7WKSPT) allows the distance between supports to be increased to 60" for heavily loaded worksurfaces, or up to 72" for lighter expected loads. Reinforcing channel must be specified separately.
Knife edge worksurfaces require reinforcement channels for unsupported spans greater than 48": TS7WKSPT39 for 54"W, TS7WKSPT for 60"W and 66"W, TS7WKSPT72 for 72"W worksurfaces.
Soft edge worksurfaces and power and data access door and tray worksurfaces require reinforcement channel or other support on worksurfaces 60" or larger.
On-module supports can be used to panel support worksurfaces in various configurations; they engage the slots in the vertical uprights of Answer panels.
Worksurface supports feature an alignment tab used to set a depth for Universal Systems Worksurfaces with 1/2" cord drop. This tab is bent down when installing full-depth worksurfaces.
Cantilever can panel-support a worksurface at any height. End panel can support the end of a worksurface. Center support panel can be shared by two worksurfaces and may be required for longer runs.

Side support brackets support the ends of straight and corner worksurfaces and the back corner of any corner worksurface; support worksurfaces at any height in 1" increments; ship as a left- and right-hand pair and are ordered separately. They can support the end of a worksurface wrapped by a panel with the same width dimension that matches the worksurface depth.

Single side support bracket can support the rear corner of corner, extended corner, and 120° corner worksurfaces, and the user's side rear corner of bullet peninsula, angled peninsula, visitor, jetty, and bubble jetty worksurfaces. Tip: For off-module fin wall applications, the single side support bracket must be handed appropriately for connection to the fin wall.

Cantilevers support worksurfaces at any height in 1" increments; cantilever is non-handed and can support either end of a worksurface, or be shared to support two worksurfaces at the same height simultaneously. One tie plate ships with each cantilever.

Adjacent cantilevered worksurfaces must be the same height in order to connect with a tie plate and provide panel stability. Tip: Answer panel junctions can accommodate only one support at each worksurface seam.

Center support panel is an alternative to a cantilever in supporting longer runs of worksurfaces for additional panel stability. Center support panels are available in seated and standing heights, cannot be used in freestanding applications or as a substitute for an end panel. One tie plate ships with each center support panel.

Center support panels should not be installed along the user's edge on P-edge profile jetty and visitor worksurfaces (unfinished top edge exposed). Use single side support bracket and a post or cabby leg.
End panels can support the end of a worksurface for additional panel stability; available in seated and standing heights, and cannot be used in freestanding applications.

Pedestals and lateral files with a filler can support the end of a worksurface in place of an end panel. All panel mounted supports can be removed and repositioned later without permanent damage to panels or skins.

Off-module worksurface-to-panel connector connects 18"D, 24"D, and 30"D worksurfaces to wider panels, eliminating the need to match panel width to worksurface depth. Replaces side supports, cantilevers, and the need for front edge support with 30"D worksurfaces. Connector attaches into the slotted channels of the panel junctions.
Worksurface can be positioned anywhere along the width of the off-module connector.
Off-module worksurface to panel connector cannot be used at the same elevation on adjacent inline panels.
Off-module worksurface to panel connector can support a single worksurface only.
Off-module worksurface to panel connector cannot replace cantilevers and side support brackets when worksurface is parallel to the panel.

27"H fixed pedestals are floor-standing and support worksurfaces at 28 1/2"H; the 3"H base is integral to the 27"H case and gives base alignment with other Universal Storage components that have a 3"H base.
Fixed pedestal top is open and accommodates attachment to a worksurface; attachment hardware is included.
Lock is standard on pedestals and secures all drawers; lock is located in the top drawer; standard factory-installed, keyed random.
Leveling glides: 25 1/2"H pedestals have a 7/8" adjustable glide range; 27"H pedestals have a 1 7/8" adjustable glide range.

Flush-front pedestal pull is full width and integral, available on steel drawer fronts only. Full-width wood pull is an option; it ships separately and is field installed with double-sided tape to the integral pull.

File drawers accommodate front-to-back filing of hanging letter-size folders; optional rails accommodate side-to-side filing of letter-, A4-, and legal-size folders. Exception: legal-size file folders cannot be filed in 17 1/2"D (printed ambiguously as 17 1/8 or 17 7/8) or 18 3/8"D pedestals; only 22 5/8, 23 1/2, 28 5/8 and 29 1/2"D pedestals accommodate legal-size filing (tip p.609).

Mobile pedestal casters are hard composition, non-locking, full-rotation swivel; casters exposed at base of box/file pedestals and concealed on box/box/file and file/file. Top on mobile pedestal is 1/8"H steel; additional top options available.
Mobile pedestal cushion top provides a temporary seat; optional handle; available factory- or field-installed.

Actual dimensions: fixed depth 17 1/2, 22 5/8, 28 5/8" (flush) / 18 3/8, 23 1/2, 29 1/2" (proud steel or wood), width 15", height 25 1/2" and 27"; mobile box/file and box/box/file & file/file depths 17 1/2 & 22 5/8" (flush) / 18 3/8 & 23 1/2" (proud); overall height with 1/8"H top: box/file 21", box/box/file and file/file 27".
Pencil tray is included with each box/box/file pedestal. Optional basic drawer interior allows box/box/file pedestals to be ordered without rails, box drawer dividers, or pencil trays.
Proud-front pulls: contemporary, handle, jazz, bar (each 128 mm) on steel or wood veneer drawers; c:scape pulls (200 mm) on steel drawers only.
Safety interlock system allows only one drawer to be opened at a time.
Individual drawer locks are available on file/file pedestals only and are only available with field-installed lock cylinders. Non-locking pedestal is an option.
Top options on mobile pedestals in place of standard 1/8"H steel top: 1"H steel, 1 3/16"H laminate square edge, 1 7/16"H laminate with bullnose front edge, 1 3/16"H wood veneer square edge.
Mobile pedestal cushion top for field installation can be used with RPM2421CP, RPM2421CF and RPM2421CW only.

Fixed pedestals are intended to attach under a worksurface; three depths correspond with Universal Worksurface depths; proud-front pedestals exactly match worksurface depth, flush-front pedestals are 7/8" shorter.

Filler conceals gap between panel face and back of a 27"H pedestal and provides stability for pedestal/worksurface configurations that are not panel-wrapped. Fillers for proud front pedestals conceal a 1/2" gap; fillers for flush front pedestals conceal a 1 3/8" gap.
Pedestals may require counterweights when used in stand-alone desks (see Desk Stability Guidelines, page 124).
Freestanding applications that don't require attachment to a worksurface should use a conversion kit (steel top, counterweight package, components to convert locking system to safety interlock).
Fixed pedestals do not accommodate cable-routing; plan accordingly under worksurfaces with grommets or other cable-routing accessories.
